title: [CVSS 8.1 HIGH] CVE-2026-126716 — The Mega Forms – Drag & Drop Form Builder with Multi-Step & Conditional Logic …
summary: The Mega Forms – Drag & Drop Form Builder with Multi-Step & Conditional Logic plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the delete_entry function in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.9 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). The attacker-supplied path is stored via the unauthenticated form submission endpoint, but the actual file deletion only occurs when an administrator subsequently deletes the stored entry — a routine housekeeping action that serves as the detonation trigger. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

title: [CVSS 8.8 HIGH] CVE-2026-125085 — The Nexter Extension – Security, Performance, Code Snippets & Site Toolkit plu…
summary: The Nexter Extension – Security, Performance, Code Snippets & Site Toolkit plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in versions up to, and including, 4.9.0 This is due to the role_switcher_to_view_admin_as() function handling the `reset-view` branch without a capability check or nonce when the caller's own login is supplied, combined with an incomplete cleanup hook (maybe_prevent_switchback_to_administrator) that exits early when the user's current roles equal the stored view role and that is never triggered when WordPress core's WP_User::set_role() short-circuits because the account already has only the target role. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to elevate their privileges to Administrator.

A nonce sufficient to pass the initial nonce check is publicly exposed on any board listing page, meaning no prior authentication or privileged access is required to initiate the exploit.

summary: The Toocheke Companion plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Missing Authorization leading to arbitrary post and attachment deletion in versions up to, and including, 2.38. This is due to a missing object-level capability check in the toocheke_tapas_ajax_cleanup_start() and toocheke_tapas_ajax_cleanup_step() AJAX handlers; the toocheke_tapas_cleanup_ajax_guard() method only verifies the primitive delete_posts capability (held by every Contributor) and never calls current_user_can('delete_post', $post_id) or delete_others_posts before passing the attacker-supplied series_post_id to wp_delete_post() and wp_delete_attachment() with force-delete enabled. The required nonce is emitted on the Import: Tapas admin page, which is gated only by edit_posts, so a Contributor can read it. summary: Flyto2 Core is an execution kernel for automation and AI-agent workflows. Prior to 2.26.8, the earlier CVE-2026-67429 remediation applied validate_path_with_env_config() to only a hand-picked set of file-writing modules, leaving data.csv.write in src/core/modules/atomic/data/csv_write.py, data.json_to_csv in src/core/modules/atomic/data/json_to_csv.py, file.copy in src/core/modules/atomic/file/copy.py, and file.move in src/core/modules/atomic/file/move.py outside the FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR confinement boundary. The advisory also identifies unguarded modules across the broader data.*, file.*, and report-writer families. data.csv.write relies on a .. substring denylist that does not reject absolute paths, while the other named modules accept caller-controlled output or destination paths without the canonical guard. A caller able to execute modules or recipes can therefore write attacker-controlled content outside the configured sandbox, potentially overwriting application code, recipes, startup files, scheduled-task files, or authorization files and gaining code execution on the host. This issue is fixed in version 2.26.8.

title: [CVSS 8.8 HIGH] CVE-2026-133476 — In Dolibarr before 24.0.3, dolForgeSQLCriteriaCallback() in htdocs/core/lib/func…
summary: In Dolibarr before 24.0.3, dolForgeSQLCriteriaCallback() in htdocs/core/lib/functions.lib.php allows account takeover because it strips only a single table-name prefix from a Universal Search Filter (sqlfilters) operand before checking it against the forbidden-field denylist (pass, pass_crypted, api_key). MariaDB and MySQL accept a two-level qualification such as schema.alias.column, so an operand of the form dolibarr.u.pass_crypted survives the check and is emitted into the WHERE clause. A remote authenticated user holding only the holiday read and readall permissions, which confer no user-management or administrative access, can use the resulting boolean oracle at GET /api/index.php/holidays to recover any user's bcrypt password hash and api_key one character at a time, including an administrator's. Because api_key is accepted directly by the REST API as a bearer credential, this yields full administrative control of the application. This bypasses the fix for CVE-2026-89012, which added only a strtolower() call and did not address prefix depth. The same denylist also omits pass_temp, which stores a password in cleartext, as well as national_registration_number, salary, birth, address, personal_mobile and note_private.

title: [CVSS 9.8 CRITICAL] CVE-2026-114516 — Etherpad is a real-time collaborative editor. From 1.8.14 until 3.3.3, the pre-a…
summary: Etherpad is a real-time collaborative editor. address of the other customer, and depending on the shop configuration
further contact data, then appear in the order confirmation and customer
account. As the IDs are sequential, addresses can be enumerated. Goods may
also be shipped to the wrong address.

summary: The WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0 and 6.17.0, respectively, via deserialization of untrusted input during database restore and staging reset. This is due to the database importer treating attacker-controlled text beginning with {WPSTG_BINARY} as trusted internal binary data and decoding its hexadecimal suffix into serialized bytes. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to plant a malicious serialized object in their own profile. When an Administrator later performs an ordinary database-including restore or staging reset containing that value, and the restored profile metadata is loaded, either during the restore or in a later request, a built-in POP chain can be used to execute arbitrary code on the server. Additional built-in gadget chains allow arbitrary local file read in both WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro and arbitrary file deletion in WP STAGING Pro. The attacker does not require Administrator credentials or a copy of a backup, but exploitation does require the later privileged restore or reset.
